LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing (2 Sessions) • Punctuation mark
Topic 3.7: Guided Writing: Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Creative Writing, part of Writing 3.5 Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing (2 Sessions) • Punctuation mark in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can you make a story more interesting in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop interest in artistic expression through writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. construct simple sentences using acquired vocabulary,

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write creative texts on the theme using descriptive words,

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop interest in artistic expression through writing.

   Guided Writing: Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to audio recording and write vocabulary related to the theme,

2. form sentences using descriptive words about feelings and emotions in small groups,

3. share the sentences with their peers for review, e.g I am hungry today

4. compose a simple story using vocabulary based on the theme,

5. identify verbs from texts, in pairs,

6. play a game of forming verbs from jumbled up letters .

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to audio recording and write vocabulary related to the theme,
2. form sentences using descriptive words about feelings and emotions in small groups,
3. share the sentences with their peers for review, e.g I am hungry today
4. compose a simple story using vocabulary based on the theme,
5. identify verbs from texts, in pairs,
6. play a game of forming verbs from jumbled up letters .

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem solving: These are promoted as the learner analyses concepts to form sentences using

descriptive words about feelings and emotions in small groups.

• Digital literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with digital materials when listening to audio recordings and writing

vocabulary related to the theme.

51

Values:
Love: This is promoted as the learner displays trustworthiness when playing a game of forming verbs from jumbled up letters.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self awareness: This is promoted as the learner is encouraged to accept their feelings and emotions, and express them

confidently.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of writing stories to their learning of creative texts in English and Kiswahili.
